why: Each warehouse has a fixed price in co-worker skips that makes you land the final dispatch, and every warehouse is worth exactly 1 credit. With a shared skip budget, buy the cheapest warehouses first: sort the prices and take them while the budget lasts.
hints: Warehouses are independent apart from the shared skip budget, and each one is worth the same 1 credit.

One full round removes dispatch1 + dispatch2. Let r = the remainder left for the last round, r = (inventory - 1) mod (d1 + d2) + 1. If r <= d1 you finish it for free; otherwise you need ceil(r / d1) - 1 extra turns of yours, each paid for by one skip.
Compute that cost per warehouse in O(1), sort the costs, and take the cheapest ones while the budget covers them. O(n log n).
pitfalls: Inventory that is an exact multiple of d1 + d2: the remainder is d1 + d2, not 0, so use (v - 1) mod s + 1.
Skipping is pointless before the last round; only the remainder matters, so never simulate turn by turn (values up to 10^9).
skips can be up to 10^9 and may cover every warehouse; the answer is then n.
